content.text: {"abstained": false, "abstention_reason": "", "answer": "The National Bamboo Mission (NBM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2018-19 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare [E02]. It was restructured following a 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act that excluded bamboo from the definition of tree [E02]. The scheme focuses on developing the complete value chain of the bamboo sector, from planting material and plantation to processing, marketing, and brand building [E02]. Key objectives include increasing bamboo plantation area on non-forest lands to supplement farm income and support climate resilience, improving post-harvest management, promoting product development, rejuvenating the bamboo industry, promoting skill development, and reducing dependency on bamboo imports [E02]. The scheme targets farmers, government agencies, artisans, entrepreneurs, private agencies, and other persons involved in the bamboo industry [E01]. It provides assistance for establishing bamboo nurseries, cultivation, post-harvest processing, product manufacturing, capacity building, and entrepreneurship [E01].
